input.question: besides the dollar amount, what the hell are autioneers actually saying?
input.ground_truth: It doesn't really matter what they're saying. The point is to get you psyched up and excited so you're more prone to buying something. All about energy levels moreso than actual content. If you go to some auctions for more expensive items (luxury cars, art, etc.), then you'll probably hear a slower auctioneer and a more thorough description of the item.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friend are playing a game where you take turns saying bigger and bigger numbers for a toy you both want. An "auctioneer" is like the person running the game. They don't just say the price ("$10! $15! $20!"), they also say things like:

- "Do I hear more?" (They want to know if anyone will pay more money.)
- "Going once, going twice…" (They're about to give the toy to the highest bidder if no one says a higher number.)
- "Sold!" (Someone won and has to buy the toy for the last price said.)
- "Who's next?" (They want another friend to try to win the toy by saying a bigger number.)

So, besides saying the money numbers, the auctioneer is asking questions and telling everyone what's happening in the game, so everyone knows when to talk and who wins the toy.
